Addario’s career took a significant turn when she
went to Afghanistan in 2000. Her photographs
captured the grief, resilience, and courage of
Afghan women.
(A) Time and again, however, she has risked her life
to capture images that speak volumes about the
suffering of those ⓐ[catching / caught] in the
conflicts between nations.
“The idea of me going to a war zone was out
of the question. ㉠그때 9.11 테러가 왔고, 이건
내가 취재해야 할 것만 같은 생각이 들었던 결정
적인 역사적 순간이었어요.
(B) This body of work gained international recognition,
ⓑ[served / serving] as a stepping stone for
Addario’s future achievements. Over the years,
Addario’s work has taken her to many regions
torn by war, including Iraq, Sudan, Libya, and
Syria. She knows very well what could happen in
the wars: she was captured twice and was even
threatened with her life.
(C) From there I ended up covering the war in Iraq
in 2003 because again, I felt like I needed to
be there. Young soldiers of my generation were
going in to fight, and I thought it was
important to document the war. I’m lucky
because I’ve survived. I’m now at the point in
my life and my career ⓒ[which / where] many
of my friends are not. And so I think it’s
important to realize there is a reason I’m still
here, and I have to keep pushing forward.”

I have found that nothing in life is of value (A)[if /
unless] you take risks. Nothing. Now I’m sure in
your experiences in school, in applying to college,
in picking your major, in deciding what you want to
do with life, people have told you to make sure
you have something to “fall back on.” But I never
understood that concept, having something to fall
back on. If I’m going to fall, I don’t want to fall
back on anything. I want to fall forward. This is
what I mean. Reggie Jackson struck out 2,600 times
in his career, the most in the history of baseball.
But you don’t hear about it. People remember the
home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 (B)[failed / successful] experiments because
the 1,001st was the light bulb. Fall forward. Every
failed experiment is one step closer to success.
You’ve got to take risks. I want to talk to you
about why that’s so important. You will fail at some
point in your lives. You will lose. You will embarrass
yourselves. There is no doubt about it. I know
that’s probably not a traditional message for a
graduation ceremony but I’m telling you. Embrace it
because it’s (C)[avoidable / inevitable].

In the acting business, you fail all the time. Early
on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting smaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job. But
here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back. I
walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So

on in my career, I auditioned for a part in a
Broadway musical. A perfect role for me, I thought,
except for the fact that I can’t sing. So I’m in the
wings. I’m about to go on stage but the guy in
front of me, he’s singing like Pavarotti, and I’m just
getting smaller and smaller. I didn’t get the job. But
here’s the thing. I didn’t quit. I didn’t fall back. I
walked out of there to prepare for the next
audition and the one after that. I continued to fail
and fail, but it didn’t matter. There is an old saying:
if you hang around the barbershop long enough,
sooner or later you’re going to get a haircut. So
you will catch a break, which is exactly what I did.

것이 중요하다 고 생각했기 때문에 그 전쟁을 취재했다. 17) ⑤: ⓑ ‘dedicate oneself to+-ing’는 ‘~하는 데 전념하다’라 는 뜻의 표현으로, 전치사 to 뒤에 동명사 throwing이 오는 것이 적절하다. ⓓ ‘by+-ing’는 ‘~함으로써’라는 뜻으로 방법·수단을 나 타내므로, ‘~을 잡아냄으로써’라는 뜻의 By 회복력 과 희망의 순간까지 조명해 왔고, 뉴스 사진 분야에서 가장 영향력 있고 존경받는 인물 중 하나라는 점을 설 명한다. 따라서 주제로는 ④ ‘분쟁과 위기를 취재하는 사진작가의 활동과 영향’이 가장 적절하다. 오답 ① 주요 세계적 위기를 기록해 온 보도 사진의 역사 ② 사진이 위기에 처한 사람들의 회복력과 희망을 드러 내는 방식 ③ 영향력 있고 존경받는 전문 보도 사진작가가 되는 방법 ⑤ 고난과 고통의 시기에 드러나는 인간성의 의미 19) ①: (A) 위험을 감수해야 한다는 주장을 전개하고 있으므로, ‘위험을 감수하지 않는다면 인생에서 가치 있는 것은 아무것도 없다’라는 의미가 되도록 ‘~하지 않는 한’을 뜻하는 unless가 알맞다. (B) Edison의 1,001번째 실험에서 비로소 전구가 만들 어졌다고 했으므로, 그보다 앞선 1,000번의 실험은 원 하는 결과를 얻지 못한 실험이었다는 것을 알 수 있다. 뒤에서도 ‘모든 실패한 실험은 성공에 한 걸음 더 가까 워지는 것’이라고 하며 이러한 실패의 의미를 강조하고 있으므로 failed가 알맞다. (C) 누구나 삶의 어느 시점에서는 실패하고, 패배하고, 창피를 당하게 된다고 하면서 이를 받아들이라고 말하고 있으므로, ‘피할 수 없는’을 뜻하는 inevitable이 알맞다. 20) ⑤: 화자는 위험을 감수하지 않으면 인생에서 가치 있는 것 은 없다고 하며, 뒤를 받쳐 줄 무언가를 두기보다 앞으 로 넘어지라고 말한다. Reggie Jackson과 Thomas Edison의 예를 통해 모든 실패가 성공에 한 걸음 더 다 가가는 것임을 강조하고, 실패는 불가피하므로 받아들 이라고 한다. 따라서 요지로 가장 적절한 것은 ⑤ '실패 를 발판 삼아 성공을 향해 나아가야 한다'이다. 오답 ① 위험을 감수하기 전에 항상 뒤를 받쳐 줄 것을 준비 해야 한다. ② 위대한 업적은 수많은 시련을 극복한 결과물이다. ③ 젊은 시절의 다양한 경험은 인생의 소중한 자산이다. ④ 인생에서 실패의 가능성을 최소화하는 지혜가 요구 된다. 21) ②: 화자는 브로드웨이 뮤지컬 오디션에서 떨어진 뒤에도 포기하지 않고 계속 도전했고, 거듭된 실패 끝에 결국 기회를 잡았다. 즉, 실패를 피하는 것이 아니라 실패하 더라도 계속 나아가는 태도가 중요하다는 내용이므로, 빈칸에는 ② ‘실패할 용기’가 가장 적절하다. 오답 ① 재능을 알아보는 안목 ③ 경쟁하려는 의욕 ④ 실패를 피하는 능력 ⑤ 성공할 자신감 22) ③: 화자는 브로드웨이 뮤지컬 오디션에서 떨어진 뒤에도 포기하거나 물러서지 않고, 다음 오디션과 그다음 오디 션을 계속 준비하며 도전을 이어 갔다. 따라서 ③ ‘오 디션에 실패한 뒤, 화자는 브로드웨이 배역에 더 이상 도전하지 않기로 했다.’는 윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않 는다. 오답 ① 화자는 노래를 잘하지 못했음에도 한때 브로드웨이 뮤지컬 오디션을 보았다. ② 자신의 앞에 있던 남자가 노래하는 것을 듣고 화자 는 오디션 전에 자신감이 줄어들었다. ④ 화자는 거듭된 실패를 겪은 뒤에도 계속 다음 오디 션들을 준비했다. ⑤ 수십 년 후 화자는 과거에 오디션에서 떨어졌던 바 로 그 극장에서 공연했다.

home runs. Fall forward. Thomas Edison conducted
1,000 failed experiments because the 1,001st was

important. You will fail at some point in your lives.

Changes in visual designs can markedly affect
behaviors of people, especially on streets. Two artists,
mother and daughter, painted a 3D crosswalk on
several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, ⓐcausing
them to slow down without braking too suddenly.
The scheme was also adopted in Delhi, India. This,
in turn, inspired Ralf Trylla, an environmental
commissioner in Iceland, to head a similar project.
As a result, drivers ⓑwere being more careful at
intersections, which reduced accidents and elevated
the safety of pedestrians. The idea has been well
received and ⓒmirrored in cities of China, the U.S.,
Canada, and the UK as well.
Likewise, traffic engineers design pavement markings
on the roads that drive people ⓓto change their
behavior without realizing it. Chicago was one of
the first U.S. cities to experiment with this idea. In
2006, it painted a series of lines across the road
ahead of a dangerous curve on North Lake Shore
Drive. The lines are spaced in such a way that as
the road nears the curve, the gaps between the
lines get smaller and smaller. This gives drivers
approaching the curve an illusion ⓔwhich they are
speeding up, which prompts them to step on the
brakes. Chicago traffic engineers reported a 36%
reduction in crashes at the North Lake Shore Drive
curve in the first six months after painting the lines.
Since then, the Chicago Department of Transportation
has painted the gapped lines at similar curves.

A default is defined as an option that applies if
the chooser does nothing. Of course, the chooser
has the freedom to opt out of the default. Defaults
are effective at nudging people toward more
desirable behaviors. Human beings are subject to a
powerful desire ㉠_____________________________________
because making a change requires a conscious
effort. Furthermore, because a default also gives the
impression that someone is recommending this
choice, if people choose to opt out, they might feel
they are not being good citizens, particularly in the
case of green defaults.
Setting
greener
choices
as
defaults
can
automatically nudge people into more sustainable
behaviors. In 2008, Rutgers University instituted a
new student printing policy to save on paper waste:
it established printing on both sides of paper as
the default setting for all its printers. As a result of
that simple change, the university saved about 62
million sheets of paper in about three years.

food delivery app. A company recently announced
an update for its app where it would change the
default settings for the optional items, such as
forks, spoons, and straws. Users would have to opt
out of the default to get them. The company
mentioned in an online post that ⓐhas surveyed
many of its customers, they found that more than
90% of them didn’t really need disposable plastic
items with their orders.

behavior? Then why not nudge them in the right
direction? There are many ways to subtly influence
people to make better decisions. As we are all
choice architects every now and then, ⓑit pays
knowing how to set people on the right path.

on several roads in Ahmedabad, India. To motorists,
the painted lines look like roadblocks, causing them
to slow down without braking too suddenly.

Dark patterns are design elements or processes
that

behavior. They come in a wide variety of forms.
Sometimes they are harmless, but sometimes they
are misleading. The following examples of dark
patterns will help you recognize and deal with them
properly in the future.
Forced Continuity
If you have signed up for a streaming service
recently, you have probably run into this dark
pattern where your credit card is automatically
charged as soon as a free trial comes to an end.
While the companies that do this would argue that
it enables users to continue to access their service
uninterrupted, users receive no warning that their
cards are about to be charged, often causing them
to be billed unexpectedly. This method is used by
many streaming platforms, but it is also common
with other services that offer free trials.
Artificial Scarcity
“Only two pieces available!” “Only four hours left
until the offer ends!” “Only ten slots left for this
program!” Artificial scarcity is used to stimulate
purchases. This typically comes in three major
forms: insufficient quantities, time, or availability. We
make decisions more quickly under pressure. The
decision is then often made quite automatically only
on the basis of scarcity. After all, no one wants to
miss out on a great offer.
Hidden Information
In this pattern, important information and options
are hidden or displayed in such a way that they are
hardly noticeable. To see the information, you have
to click somewhere, look very closely, or actively
search for it.
Every newsletter must allow you to unsubscribe.
